minutes.headline: Committee approved stipend and coaching schedules and an SRO agreement, and told the athletic director to study middle school sports.
minutes.summary: The School Committee approved line-item transfers, a reconciling transfer for staffing surpluses and deficits, an SRO memorandum, advisor stipend and coaching salary schedules, and let the athletic director study middle school sports. It also heard a first budget report and a grant update. A resident challenged the transfers and new hiring in public comment, and several policies were read, with some pulled for edits.

public_comment.topic: Questioned the petition and public participation policy changes, the budget transfers, new hiring and paraprofessionals, and urged a long-term cash flow review.

Authorize superintendent to sign the SRO memorandum of understanding

Approve the athletic coaching salary schedule as proposed

decisions.decision: Athletic director to study middle school sports, costs and fees and report in spring; no program approved.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved the advisor stipend list as presented; the vote tally was not audible in the recording.
The Committee approved the athletic coaching salary schedule as proposed, after approving a budget line item transfer as presented.
The Committee authorized the athletic director to study middle school sports, costs and fees and report in spring; no program was approved.
The Committee authorized the superintendent to sign a memorandum of understanding for a school resource officer (SRO).
A resident questioned the budget transfers, new hiring and paraprofessionals in public comment, and urged a long-term cash flow review.

why_it_matters: Stipend and coaching pay schedules and the staffing transfers draw on the school budget, which is funded mostly by taxes, so they bear on what the district asks for in later years.
A middle school sports program, if later proposed, would add costs or student fees; this meeting only began the study.
